children: Amazon and Wiwynn are working to expand the Taiwanese server manufacturer's facility in Texas to meet growing demand from U.S. customers.

The move, which brings Wiwynn's total investment in the facility to more than $1.6 billion, will help to bolster domestic manufacturing capacity for Amazon's data center infrastructure, the companies said Wednesday.
The facility "shows what's possible when we work with our manufacturers to strengthen the U.S. supply chain," said Gary Szilagyi, Amazon's vice president of its Annapurna Labs division.

The companies expect their expanded relationship to create nearly 1,000 new advanced manufacturing jobs by the end of next year. The facility in Sorocco, Texas, which is outside El Paso along the Mexico border, will also serve customers beyond Amazon. It will employ more than 2,500 next year, and an expected 4,000 at full capacity, the companies said.

The move comes as Amazon and other hyperscalers race to scale up production of custom AI hardware, and bring more of their supply chains to the U.S. as the Trump administration pushes to rebuild American manufacturing.

Wiwynn is one of several Taiwanese companies looking to expand their U.S. manufacturing footprints to meet the rising demand. Wistron opened a $700 million facility in Texas earlier this year to produce AI "superchips" for Nvidia, and contract chip maker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing has also said it would invest an additional $100 billion in Arizona.

"Through our over $1.6 billion investment in the Texas facility, we are expanding our ability to address the growing demand of U.S. customers," Wiwynn's President and Chief Executive William Lin said.
